security_audit.summary: All 40 external-command detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around workflow names, field names, and status values. The system-reconnaissance detection is also a false positive because it describes evidence practices in prose; no executable security threat was evidenced in the supplied findings.

remediation.issue: Static matching treats Markdown backticks as Ruby or shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict the external-command rule to executable code blocks or parsed command syntax, and ignore inline Markdown code spans.

remediation.issue: The system-reconnaissance rule flags ordinary descriptions of test evidence.
remediation.suggestion: Require actual host or environment inspection operations before reporting reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Teams can lose requirements when agent-skill work moves from planning to implementation and review. This skill keeps requirements, acceptance evidence, review state, and completion claims connected through a clear traceability process.
actual_capabilities: Map requirements to acceptance items, user journeys, increments, and verification evidence.
Separate host-native lifecycle outcomes from worker checks and advisory guidance.
Track review, continuation, and release states without treating incomplete evidence as success.
Define incremental delivery groups and explicit stop, await-owner, or host-boundary actions.
Preserve current test and host status claims independently from reused evidence.
limitations: It provides a process framework, not an execution engine for builds, reviews, or deployments.
It cannot verify test results or host state without current evidence from the host environment.
It does not replace project-specific requirements, security review, or release approval.
It depends on accurate source requirements and consistent evidence records.

use_cases.title: Plan an agent-skill feature
use_cases.description: Convert a feature brief into traceable requirements, acceptance items, increments, and verification gates.

use_cases.title: Review incremental implementation
use_cases.description: Check that each completed increment has current evidence, correct review status, and no unsupported completion claims.

use_cases.title: Prepare a controlled release
use_cases.description: Separate build completion from review, shipping, deployment, and post-launch verification before release decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a traceability plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this feature brief into requirements, acceptance items, user journeys, and verification steps. Keep each item uniquely identifiable.

prompt_templates.title: Map one increment
prompt_templates.prompt: For this increment, map every change to requirement IDs and acceptance item IDs. List the evidence needed before marking it complete.

prompt_templates.title: Audit completion claims
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these implementation and test receipts. Identify unsupported completion claims, stale evidence, missing review states, and required follow-up actions.

prompt_templates.title: Define release boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a traceability-aware release plan for this production change. Separate build, review, ship, deployment, and post-launch verification, and specify when to stop or await owner approval.

output_examples.input: A request to add password reset with email delivery and audit logging.
output_examples.output: Requirements map: password reset flow, email delivery, audit event, and failure handling. Each item has acceptance checks, evidence requirements, and a named verification gate.

output_examples.input: A completed increment with unit tests passing but no current review receipt.
output_examples.output: Status: implementation evidence present; review remains pending. Action: obtain a current review receipt before claiming the increment is fully complete.

output_examples.input: A release plan that combines deployment with code review.
output: Build completion is tracked separately from review approval.
Deployment and post-launch verification remain distinct release gates.

best_practices: Use stable requirement and acceptance identifiers throughout planning, implementation, and review.
Record current evidence and host status separately from reusable historical evidence.
Make continuation actions explicit, and stop at host boundaries unless the user approved the scope.
anti_patterns: Do not infer release completion from a finished task or passing local test.
Do not copy mutable host tracker status into a separate traceability document.
Do not silently translate review severities or omit required findings during synthesis.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It keeps requirements connected to implementation, verification evidence, review state, and completion decisions.

faq.question: Does it run builds or deployments?
faq.answer: No. It defines traceability and decision boundaries; the host tools perform execution.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when planning or reviewing multi-step agent-skill work with acceptance criteria and evidence requirements.

faq.question: How does it handle stale evidence?
faq.answer: It keeps reused evidence separate and requires a fresh host gate or current status claim when needed.

faq.question: Can it authorize automatic continuation?
faq.answer: Only an explicitly approved scope can permit continuation; otherwise the process records stop or await-owner.

faq.question: Does completion imply release readiness?
faq.answer: No. Task and increment closure remain separate from review, shipping, deployment, and post-launch verification.
